q: I opened a project a colourist graded and want to learn how they built the look. How do I see what each node does?
a: 1. Select a graded clip: the Nodes panel shows its chain, 01, 02 … in the order they apply. 2. In the Match tab click Explain grade (`grade.explainGrade`): one measured sentence per node (how much of the frame it affects, which tones move and how far). 3. Select a node and click Explain node (`grade.explainNode`), then Show what changed for a heat map of where it acts. 4. Switch nodes off one at a time (Disable, `grade.toggleNode`, or double-click its box) and watch the picture; Bypass (`grade.bypass`) flips the whole grade off and on for a before / after. Then rebuild it yourself on another clip: that's how the order and amounts stick.

q: what is node 3 even doing in this grade i got, cant see any difference
a: Select node 3 and click Explain node in the Match tab (`grade.explainNode`): it measures the change on the frame at the playhead and says, for example, that it affects 18 % of the frame and lifts the midtones inside it; a change below what you'd notice is called untouched. Show what changed draws where it acts. If it only touches a small area (a window or a qualifier), park on a frame where that area is visible, then toggle the node (`grade.toggleNode`) to see it.

q: The grade explanations say things like 'midtones +1/6 stop, slightly less magenta'. Can it explain in simpler words for a beginner?
a: Yes, optionally, with a small AI model on your own computer: Settings ▸ Color (`app.settings.color`) ▸ AI explanations: pick a model (`ai.select`; a small one is quicker than SmolLM3 for this), Download it (`ai.download`, checked against its checksum), tick Explain nodes in plain words (`ai.setEnabled`) and click OK. Explain node then shows the measured sentence at once and replaces it with plainer words once they pass the check against the measurements (a checked badge). It works offline; the model only rewords, it never decides.

q: I got a comp template for a glitch title and want to change it, but the node graph makes no sense to me. Where do I start?
a: 1. Ask for a description: `comp.explain` (from the control channel or MCP; no button in the Compositor yet) lists, from the sources to Media Out, what each node does in its own names; read `summary`, then `lines` in order, and `unused` for nodes that change nothing. 2. Look at each node's picture: double-click it (or Show menu, `comp.viewer`) and the Program monitor shows that node's output; Show: Media Out goes back. 3. Change what you need in the node's settings under the canvas (`comp.setParam`); a Text node holds the title's text and font.

q: In Fusion I'd click through the nodes in the viewer to see how a template works. Same in Revolution's Compositor?
a: Mostly: double-click a node (or right-click ▸ View) and the Program monitor shows its output; there is one viewer, not Fusion's two. Show: Media Out (or `comp.view` with no node) returns to the finished comp; viewing never changes the result. Revolution also has a text description Fusion lacks: `comp.explain` says what each node does in flow order and lists unused nodes, from the control channel or MCP for now.
